title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Explore Bowdoin College's campus and coastal properties through these entirely free social spaces, museums, and activities available to students and the public.

cards.title: Bowdoin College Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Walker Art Building
cards.notes: Explore over 30,000 works in a landmark building. Admission is always free for students and the public. Check out the Assyrian reliefs and the iconic rotunda murals.
cards.short_summary: A historic, free-admission art museum featuring global collections from antiquity to the present.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bowdoin College Museum of Art is open to the public, and admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Visit | Bowdoin College Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. (until 8:30 p.m. on Thursdays) and Sunday 1:00 p.m.–5:00 p.m.

cards.title: Peary-MacMillan Arctic Museum
cards.subtitle: Gibbons Center for Arctic Studies
cards.notes: Visit the only museum in the lower 48 dedicated to the Arctic. See Inuit artifacts and equipment from historic polar expeditions without paying an entrance fee.
cards.short_summary: A specialized museum focused on Arctic exploration and culture with free public entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Museum is always free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Saturday 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and Sunday 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.

cards.title: Schiller Coastal Studies Center
cards.subtitle: Orr's Island Trails
cards.notes: Hike 2.5 miles of rocky shoreline and forest trails on Orr's Island. This 118-acre coastal site is open for public use daily from sunrise to sunset.
cards.short_summary: A coastal research facility with extensive hiking trails open to the public for free.
cards.evidence_claim: The Schiller campus is open for public use daily from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Parking is available at the trailhead kiosk.

cards.title: Harriet's Writing Room
cards.subtitle: 63 Federal Street
cards.notes: Step into the room where Stowe wrote Uncle Tom's Cabin. This historic space is open to the public for free tours on select afternoons.
cards.short_summary: A public commemorative space in the historic home where Harriet Beecher Stowe lived and wrote.
cards.evidence_claim: Harriet's Writing Room is open to the public... free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Typically open Thursdays and Fridays from 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. during the academic year.

cards.title: Hawthorne-Longfellow Library
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Library
cards.notes: Study in the historic hub named for Bowdoin's famous alumni. Visitors are welcome to use the collections and guest computers for free until 5:00 p.m. daily.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library offering free daytime access to visitors and students.
cards.evidence_claim: Visitors without library cards may use the in-house collections... there is no charge for this access.
cards.access_notes: Public access is available until 5:00 p.m. daily; after 5:00 p.m., a Bowdoin ID is required.

cards.title: Morrell Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student Union Hub
cards.notes: Relax in the central social hub of campus. This public space is ideal for people-watching, casual meetings, or attending free community-facing events.
cards.short_summary: A large, open social lounge in the student union used for studying and public events.
cards.evidence_claim: This is a public space and best for events that expect lots of foot traffic.
cards.source_title: Smith Union, Morrell Lounge for Events
cards.access_notes: Open daily during union hours; accessible to the public for general use and events.

cards.title: The Lantern
cards.subtitle: Glass Auditorium & Lounge
cards.notes: Study or attend a lecture in this LEED Platinum glass atrium. It serves as a transparent hub for environmental studies and community gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A striking glass-walled auditorium and common space designed for interdisciplinary gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lantern... is designed to be both a hub and refuge for the Bowdoin community.
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; frequently hosts free public lectures.

cards.title: Student Theater & Dance Performances
cards.subtitle: Memorial Hall
cards.notes: Catch high-quality student productions and dance concerts. Many Department of Theater and Dance shows are free and open to the public with a ticket.
cards.short_summary: Free admission to various student-led theater and dance performances throughout the year.
cards.evidence_claim: Most student shows offer free tickets through Bowdoin's ticketing site.
cards.source_title: Events | Department of Theater and Dance
cards.access_notes: Tickets are required but often free; check the online calendar for specific show dates.

cards.title: Young Artists Series Concerts
cards.subtitle: Kanbar Auditorium
cards.notes: Enjoy free classical music performances by talented festival students. These lively concerts are held in a state-of-the-art converted gymnasium.
cards.short_summary: A series of free classical music recitals featuring students from the International Music Festival.
cards.evidence_claim: All performances are free and are also livestreamed online.
cards.source_title: Young Artists Series - Bowdoin International Music Festival
cards.access_notes: Performances occur seasonally; check the festival calendar for summer and academic year dates.

cards.title: Bowdoin Pines
cards.subtitle: Old-Growth Forest Trails
cards.notes: Walk through one of the few remaining old-growth white pine stands in the region. The trails are located right next to the Roux Center and are free to access.
cards.short_summary: A historic grove of towering white pines with public walking paths adjacent to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Roux Center... let in natural light and views of the nearby pines.
cards.source_title: What Makes the Roux Center Building So Special?
cards.access_notes: Open to the public year-round for walking and nature observation.
